elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: The Licensee may assign without consent to an Affiliate.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The exception expressly permits assignment without consent to a successor in a merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The exception expressly permits assignment without consent to a successor in an acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The exception expressly permits assignment without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Licensor may not assign the Agreement without Licensee's prior written consent.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor's assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Licensee's consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right arising from Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: The Change of Control provision states that a Change of Control shall give Licensor no right to terminate; it also eliminates automatic termination.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Licensee may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Customer must provide written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: No written-notice obligation applies to Licensee's permitted successor assignments.

elements.element: Vendor may assign to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: There is no successor-assignment exception for Licensor; all Licensor assignments require Licensee's consent and competitor assignments are prohibited.

elements.element: Vendor must provide written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no notice-based successor-assignment mechanism for Licensor.

elements.element: Customer's assignments other than permitted successor assignments require Vendor's consent.
elements.evidence: Licensee's assignments outside the stated Affiliate and M&A-successor exceptions require Licensor's prior written consent.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to Customer's other assignments.
elements.evidence: The clause does not restrict Licensor from unreasonably withholding consent to Licensee assignments.

elements.element: Vendor's assignments other than permitted successor assignments require Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Licensor may not assign the Agreement without Licensee's prior written consent.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to Vendor's other assignments.
elements.evidence: Although the general consent language says consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, the absolute prohibition on assignments to Licensee competitors overrides that standard for a category of non-successor assignments.

result.reason: The rendered language reaches every preferred requirement: Licensee receives the specified Affiliate and M&A-successor assignment rights, Licensor assignments require consent subject to a reasonableness standard and a competitor prohibition, and Change of Control cannot trigger termination. The fallback is not fully implemented because there is no mutual successor-assignment-on-written-notice mechanism, Licensor has no consent-free successor right, and Licensor's consent to Licensee's other assignments is not subject to a reasonableness standard. The changes are confined to assignment and Change of Control, although the retained punctuation defect around “Section Subject” and the terse scope of “Licensee may assign” reduce drafting polish.
